hero.headline: Everything your agent knows, in a third of the context
hero.sub: The session-start preload had grown faster than the vault it describes. On a real mature brain it now loads at 16,320 characters instead of 48,964 — fully inline, no truncation banner, and nothing dropped. What got cut was repetition, not knowledge.

shot.caption: The shape of a brain after 0.23.0: a person, and a constitution-only soul.

blocks.title: Your brain knows who is at the keyboard
blocks.body:
The old 1.user.md was one file trying to be a person, a roster and a junk drawer. It is gone. Each person now gets their own constitution in people/, loaded verbatim when they are the one working — resolved from your git email, with nothing about your machine written into the shared brain.

Existing vaults are migrated for you: the deterministic half runs on upgrade, and the prose that needed judgement is handed to an agent rather than guessed at.

shot.alt: The Core file list: a PEOPLE heading with Mehmet Nuraydın marked active, then CORE FILES listing soul, active-decisions, style-guide, tech-stack, System Flow, CHANGELOG, RELEASES and taxonomy — with no 1.user.md among them
shot.caption: No 1.user.md. A person, then the core files.

blocks.title: Rules stopped hiding in a folder line
blocks.body:
A soul that holds every conditional rule is a soul nobody can read, and under budget pressure those rules used to collapse into an anonymous folder count. Now the conditional half lives in knowledge/patterns/ as clustered files, and patterns get their own block in every snapshot at every budget level, under a hard warning banner.

A rule can be demoted in detail. It can no longer be demoted into silence.

shot.alt: The Knowledge page with the Patterns folder expanded to 17 entries, showing pattern cards whose descriptions are the rule itself — budget demotion floor prevents blinding, build and propagate order, byte-surgical section editing — each tagged by domain
shot.caption: 17 patterns, each described by the rule it carries.

blocks.title: Two new ways to find things
lines: Changelog — page 1/185 (554 matching entries, newest first)
- 2026-07-30 [feat] cli: New dreamcontext changelog list — paginated
- 2026-07-30 [feat] snapshot: Patterns get their own block with a HARD
# recall ranks by relevance. these two answer "what happened, in order".

items.title: Memory renders in full
items.text: A memory file at or under 4,000 characters is no longer compressed at render time. Sleep is memory's compressor; doing it twice was just taxation.

items.title: Tasks are accounted for
items.text: Tasks show their real name instead of a slug. Under pressure the list becomes an accounting: detailed, named and counted always sum to the total.

items.title: Nothing is a dead end
items.text: Every inventory section carries a search-and-browse footer at every level, including its floor — so a compressed section always tells you how to reach the rest.

items.title: Turkish names survive
items.text: Accented and Turkish titles fold to ASCII before slugifying, so a name like "Öğretmen fiyatı" keeps its letters instead of being mangled.

blocks.text: This release also carries v0.22.0, which was built but never published — if you are coming from 0.21.0 you get Automations and the Chat work in the same upgrade. Its own story sits directly below this one in the feed.

One caveat worth knowing: verifying the migrations above turned up a defect where running install-skill before update could silently skip them. That is fixed in this release, and guarded by a test that fails if anyone reopens it — but it is the reason to upgrade with dreamcontext update rather than around it.

closer.title: Upgrade and let it migrate
closer.body: dreamcontext upgrade, then dreamcontext update in each project. The structural migrations run on that command, and anything needing judgement is handed to your agent with instructions.
